answer.rationale: Primary objective is sustained availability without losing customer writes. Latency is climbing and confined to the primary region. The release cannot be reverted due to compliance, so rollback_release is off the table. Settlement traffic is at peak, so adding capacity would be slow and likely insufficient against a 5x p99 spike. Circuit breakers (b4) preserve the rest of the checkout path but sacrifice writes — incompatible with the primary objective. Read replica routing (b5) addresses dashboard load, not write-path latency. Regional failover (b2) directly addresses a regional degradation: shift traffic away from the failing primary region, restore write latency, preserve all writes, and the security patch travels with the build so compliance is maintained. Verifying b2 confirms failover restored latency cleanly before, and b5 is a secondary check in case read-replica routing could offload incidental primary pressure during the cutover. With exactly one intervention available, failover is the highest-leverage choice.
